issues.issue: Is the stay motion moot because CBSA deferred the removal to August 15, 2026?
issues.applicant_position: Despite the short deferral, a live issue remains: whether removal should be stayed until the appeal is determined.
issues.result_quote: I rendered a ruling from the bench that the matter is not moot.

issues.issue: Has the applicant shown a serious issue to be determined in the underlying appeal (first prong)?
issues.applicant_position: The certified questions are neither frivolous nor vexatious, so a serious issue exists.
issues.respondent_position: Federal Court decision complies with established Charter s.7 and appellate law; no serious issue despite the certified questions.
issues.result_quote: I am satisfied that the underlying appeal raises at least one issue that is neither frivolous nor vexatious.

issues.issue: Has the applicant shown irreparable harm if removed before the appeal is decided (second prong)?
issues.applicant_position: Removal will cause irreparable harm: health care unavailable given Roma ethnicity, loss of family support, and mental health harm.
issues.respondent_position: Risks were already rejected in the PRRA; family separation and health concerns are inherent consequences of removal; evidence falls short.
issues.result_quote: the evidence does not demonstrate the existence of a real, definite, and unavoidable harm.

issues.issue: Does the balance of convenience favour a stay of removal (third prong)?
issues.applicant_position: Little or no prejudice to respondents if removal is deferred until the appeal is decided; he poses no danger and reports as required.
issues.respondent_position: Public interest in enforcing immigration law and public confidence outweighs his harm; a stay would undermine system integrity.
issues.result_quote: I find that the balance of convenience weighs in favour of the respondents.
